projects.focus: TECHO5 turns old, unlockable Echo devices into private Home Assistant voice satellites with "Linux inside, Home Assistant in charge, no Amazon cloud", replacing Fire OS with Alpine Linux and one daemon that drives the hardware directly. rows.name: What it is
rows.def: Fact: the form it takes, in a few words: replacement software on the device, an app installed on a stock OS, or a Home Assistant integration plus dashboard; name the parts if there are several

rows.name: Started
rows.def: Fact: date of the first commit (per repo if there are several)

rows.name: Releases
rows.def: Fact: latest release and its date; number of GitHub releases, with pre-releases counted separately

rows.name: License
rows.def: Fact: the license of each main part, as the repo states it; "none stated" where a repo has no license file

rows.name: Devices
rows.def: Fact: device models or device classes supported in a release; models in progress listed separately

rows.name: What runs on the device
rows.def: Fact: the OS left on the device and the project's own program(s) running on it; say if a separate server is needed

rows.name: Install
rows.def: Fact: what the user must do to install: unlock/root steps, USB or soldering, PC tool or script, APK sideload, HACS, and the host OS the tool needs

rows.name: Replaces the device's OS
rows.def: Yes: a release installs its own Linux userspace or image so that no Android/Fire OS process runs on the device; Partly: that is one of several install paths or covers only some supported models

rows.name: Works with other display or microphone apps
rows.def: Yes: documented setups where other projects' apps or satellites (browser apps, mic apps, ESPHome voice devices) act as its display or microphone; Partly: it hosts or interoperates with one other project's component

rows.name: Interface languages
rows.def: Yes: the device or app interface ships in more than one language; Partly: only some screens (for example date and weather) are translated, or the catalog exists with English only

rows.name: Porting to new hardware
rows.def: Yes: a documented path (guide, profile scripts or per-model files) for adding new device models; Partly: hardware notes or a protocol write-up only

rows.name: Home Assistant Assist satellite
rows.def: Yes: the device appears in HA as an Assist satellite on its own; Partly: only through a separate app from another project

rows.name: Follow-up listening
rows.def: Yes: listens again after a reply (HA continue_conversation) without the wake word; Partly: only after a question

rows.name: HA can start a conversation
rows.def: Yes: supports HA's start_conversation and ask_question actions; Partly: only one of the two

rows.name: On-device wake word
rows.def: Yes: the wake word is detected on the device itself; Partly: on-device detection only on some models or engines

rows.name: Custom wake word models
rows.def: Yes: users can add their own wake word model files and use them on the device; Partly: own models only through HA's server-side engine

rows.name: Two wake words, two assistants
rows.def: Yes: two wake words listened for at once, each starting its own pipeline; Partly: two words but one pipeline

rows.name: Wake word on a server
rows.def: Yes: an option to stream idle mic audio to HA or a controller so the wake word is detected there; Partly: the server only double-checks uncertain on-device wakes

rows.name: Start a turn without the wake word
rows.def: Yes: a button on the device, a screen control or an HA button starts listening; Partly: only a hardware button

rows.name: Cancel a request in progress
rows.def: Yes: a button, the wake word or an HA button cancels while the assistant listens or thinks; Partly: cancel only by voice "stop" during the reply

rows.name: Stop without the wake word
rows.def: Yes: saying "stop" (no wake word) ends a reply, timer or alarm; Partly: stopping needs the wake word first (barge-in) or works only for some sounds or engines

rows.name: Nearest device answers
rows.def: Yes: several devices hearing the same wake word settle locally so only one answers; Partly: works only with a server or only within part of the fleet/engines

rows.name: Echo cancellation
rows.def: Yes: the wake word and speech work over the device's own playback through echo cancellation; Partly: only for some sources or models

rows.name: Noise suppression
rows.def: Yes: a noise suppressor cleans mic audio sent to the assistant; Partly: only for wake scoring, or only experimental

rows.name: Mic gain and leveling
rows.def: Yes: adjustable mic gain or automatic leveling for speech sent to HA; Partly: fixed presets only

rows.name: Mic array mixing
rows.def: Yes: combines several mics (averaging, beam choice or delay-and-sum) with a user choice of mode; Partly: fixed mixing only

rows.name: External or USB microphone choice
rows.def: Yes: the user can pick an external USB or Bluetooth mic, or a channel of a mic array; Partly: a setup guide for external mics only

rows.name: End of speech detected on device
rows.def: Yes: the device itself decides when speech ends (VAD), with adjustable timing; Partly: only a choice of HA's VAD sensitivity

rows.name: Speech right after the wake word
rows.def: Yes: words said straight after the wake word, without waiting for a tone, reach HA; Partly: only with the wake sound turned off

rows.name: Replies start while being generated
rows.def: Yes: speech starts before the full TTS reply is ready (streamed); Partly: streaming only for some agents or TTS engines

rows.name: Saved voice recordings
rows.def: Yes: keeps recent request audio that can be played back or fetched; Partly: a short live replay buffer only

rows.name: Voice-turn history
rows.def: Yes: a browsable log of past turns with transcript and reply; Partly: last-turn sensors only

rows.name: Last-turn sensors in HA
rows.def: Yes: HA sensors for the last wake word or transcript and the reply; Partly: one of those

rows.name: Wake-word clips and near misses
rows.def: Yes: saves clips of wakes, false wakes or near misses for tuning or training; Partly: counts near misses without audio

rows.name: Uses the stock audio front end

rows.name: Whisper detection

rows.def: Yes: settings can be saved to a file and restored; Partly: export without restore

rows.name: Change Wi-Fi without reinstalling
rows.def: Yes: switch networks from the device, its page or its screen; Partly: only with a PC tool over USB

rows.name: Restart or reboot remotely
rows.def: Yes: restart the software or reboot the device from HA or a web page; Partly: only from the device itself

rows.name: Automatic recovery after a crash
rows.def: Yes: the app or page reloads or restarts by itself after a crash or load failure; Partly: only a manual reload button

rows.name: Recovery and way back to stock
rows.def: Yes: a documented rescue mode and a way back to the stock OS; Partly: one of the two

rows.name: List of other devices
rows.def: Yes: the device's page lists the other devices it found on the network and lets you jump to them; Partly: a list without links

rows.name: Device naming
rows.def: Yes: the device name/ID can be changed after setup; Partly: only before pairing, or a fixed generated name

rows.name: Reset or leave HA
rows.def: Yes: a factory reset or unpair action that clears the HA link for handing the device on; Partly: only by reinstalling

rows.name: Central management server
rows.def: Yes: a separate server or add-on that holds config and updates for every device; Partly: management from an HA integration or from a leader device

rows.name: Browser-based installer
rows.def: Yes: the install runs from a web browser (for example over WebUSB) with no local tools; Partly: a guided one-command installer or script on a PC

rows.name: Vendor cloud services removed
rows.def: Yes: the original vendor's assistant and cloud services are removed or blocked; n/a for apps on a stock OS; Partly: only some services disabled

rows.name: Inbound firewall
rows.def: Yes: a firewall limits inbound traffic to the ports the device serves; Partly: only some services closed by default

rows.name: Signed or encrypted device-to-device traffic
rows.def: Yes: traffic between devices (arbitration, intercom, sync) is keyed or signed; Partly: only some of it

rows.name: Login for settings and admin
rows.def: Yes: settings page or API needs a login, button approval or PIN, with rate limits on failures; Partly: login without rate limits or only for some functions

rows.name: Sendspin pairing
rows.def: Yes: only paired Music Assistant servers can play, with play-without-pairing opt-in; Partly: pairing optional and off by default

rows.name: HTTPS and certificate options
rows.def: Yes: verifies HTTPS certificates and lets the user trust a private CA or install its own certificate; Partly: only a switch to turn checks off, or an accept-once prompt

rows.name: Mic and camera indicators
rows.def: Yes: on-screen marks while mic or camera is in use, and camera off with mute; Partly: one of those

rows.name: No telemetry by default
rows.def: Yes: no analytics or crash reporting is sent by default; Partly: analytics present but off by default or only in some builds

rows.name: Kiosk lockdown
rows.def: Yes: locks the device to the app (exit PIN, system UI and button blocking, relaunch); Partly: a settings PIN or launcher role only

rows.name: User-made screen pages
rows.def: Yes: users can add their own pages, views or HTML as screens; Partly: only custom styling or templates

rows.name: Plugin system
rows.def: Yes: third-party plugins can be installed and add features, with a published SDK; Partly: user-written views, scripts or custom code without a plugin API

rows.name: Wake word training
rows.def: Yes: ships a tool that trains wake word models; Partly: a written guide to training with outside tools

rows.name: Stream deck and computer control
rows.def: Yes: the screen works as a button deck that drives OBS or a computer; Partly: buttons that call HA only

type: Replacement software on the device: Linux 6.1 image with C daemons, a web control center and a signed OTA updater; no separate server. Five repos: product, platform, kernel, UI, docs
started: LibreEcho 2026-07-27; LibreEcho-Platform repo created 2026-07-13 (history from an older kernel tree begins 2021-08-25); LibreEcho-UI 2026-08-20 (repo created 2026-07-19); LibreEcho-Docs 2026-07-16; LibreEcho-Linux repo created 2026-10-20 (carries upstream kernel history from 2005)
First-commit dates from the GitHub commit lists
releases: radar-puffin-v0.14.4, 2026-10-22: 18 releases plus 125 pre-releases (dev builds), all in the LibreEcho repo; the other four repos publish none
The oldest release is from 2026-08-21; latest dev build 2026-10-25
license: LibreEcho MIT; LibreEcho-UI MIT (vendored SBC code LGPL-2.1+); LibreEcho-Docs MIT; LibreEcho-Linux GPL-2.0 with Linux-syscall-note; LibreEcho-Platform has no license file of its own beyond the Linux COPYING (GPL-2.0) of its kernel tree, component licenses sit beside each part
Release bundles also carry third-party parts under their own licenses, including a noncommercial wake-word model
devices: Echo 2nd gen (radar_puffin) and Echo Dot 2nd gen (biscuit, experimental), both MT8163. Next candidates, not started: Echo Dot 3rd gen, Echo 3rd gen, Echo Plus 2nd gen, Echo Studio
on-device: Stock OS is gone: a LibreEcho Linux 6.1 kernel and ramfs userspace run C daemons (web, audio engine, wake word, STT/TTS, ESPHome satellite and others); no separate server needed
install: Linux PC with bash, curl, Python 3, adb, fastboot; USB fastboot (Echo 2: pogo-pin adapter or soldered USB cable; Dot: micro-USB); run the one-shot installer script; locked units need a community Amonet unlock zip the user supplies
Installer checks the zip's SHA-256 and verifies each download
os-replaced: Linux 6.1 image on both boot slots; no Android process runs
third-party-parts: Hosts one other project's component: Wyoming Whisper/Piper clients in Custom mode
ui-languages: Web control center is English only
porting: Hardware notes, a daemon-adding guide and a candidate list; no per-model porting guide
assist-satellite: ESPHome native API with Noise encryption; adopted through the ESPHome integration
follow-up: Honors HA continue_conversation at intent end
wake-word: openWakeWord ONNX model runs on the device
custom-wake: Only the bundled Alexa model; no model upload
no-wake-start: Action button 'Start listening' is a placeholder
cancel-turn: Mic mute cancels a listening turn; voice stop works during a reply
stop-word: Spoken stop is handled before any model call but follows the wake word
echo-cancel: AEC against a central playback reference; post-AEC audio feeds wake word and HA
mic-gain: Microphone gain slider, kept across reboots
mic-array: 12 fixed beams over four mics; beam follows the strongest talker; no user mode choice
end-of-speech: Silence length and maximum length adjustable in Local and Custom modes; HA mode uses HA's VAD
no-wake-gap: Audio from just before the wake detection is sent as pre-roll
streaming-replies: Local replies are spoken at the first natural break; HA TTS can start early
turn-history: Last 10 turns with transcript and reply, kept in RAM only
realtime-voice: GPT-Live speech-to-speech over a ChatGPT login is in source, hidden and not in 0.14 releases; it delegates device actions, not HA
voice-without-ha: Local STT and TTS plus a ChatGPT-subscription or OpenAI-compatible local LLM answer without HA
music-by-voice: Internet radio stations by spoken word only
chatgpt-assistant: ChatGPT device login, plus a local LLM endpoint setting
media-player: ESPHome media player entity plays announcements and media URLs
ducking: Media buses duck 12 dB under announcements and voice
sendspin: Draft pull requests add a Sendspin player for Music Assistant multiroom; not in a release
bluetooth-in: A2DP sink with AVRCP absolute volume (0.14.3)
custom-sounds: Action-button sound chosen from three bundled ones
radio: Internet radio with a station list; MP3, AAC and HLS
sleep-sounds: White, pink, brown noise and heartbeat generated on the device
sleep-timer: Sleep sounds take a minutes timer and fade
nursery-monitor: Live mic stream to browsers including iPhone Safari
speaker-tuning: Echo 2 and Dot get separate profiles; 24-bit output path
night-mode: No screen; the light ring has a night mode
announcements: HA announcements play through the ESPHome satellite
buttons: Buttons are handled on the device; volume and mute only, nothing sent to HA as events
mic-mute: Microphone mute is an HA switch entity
light-sensor: TSL2540 lux shown in the web UI, not an HA entity
led-ring: Ring is set from the web UI and API only; the ESPHome satellite exposes just a media player and a mic-mute switch
ring-styles: Colors and brightness per state (listening, thinking, error, DND); idle and sleep-light modes
dnd: A 'dnd' ring color profile exists but nothing in source sets it; no DND switch
health-sensors: CPU, memory, temperature and Wi-Fi on the Overview page
ring-visualizer: 12-band levels, beat and mood analysis drive the ring; switchable
ha-link: Encrypted ESPHome native API (Noise), mDNS discovery
settings-entities: Settings live in the web UI; HA sees a media player and a mute switch
timers: HA voice timers ring on the device; local timers also work
ha-down: Radio, AirPlay and Bluetooth run on the device; HA-owned timers need HA
ota: Check and install from Settings; manual .tar upload; optional automatic updates
update-rollback: Previous signed generation kept until the new one boots and confirms
signed-updates: Ed25519-signed manifests; manual uploads signature-checked by default
logs: Log viewer and live stream in the web UI
remote-shell: Optional SSH, off until switched on in the web UI, signed in with the web accounts
remote-api: Authenticated HTTP API with OpenAPI file, CSRF and Origin checks
restart: Reboot and shutdown from the web UI
auto-recover: Watchdog restarts adapter daemons that stop answering
recovery: Fastboot and recovery button modes are documented; no way back to the stock OS found
rename: Hostname can be changed after setup with PUT /api/v1/network
reset-unpair: Factory reset in the web UI
controller: Each device is managed on its own
browser-install: One-command installer script for Linux; no browser install
vendor-services-off: Stock firmware removed, so Amazon services are gone
admin-auth: Login with salted-hash accounts, CSRF and Origin checks, login rate limit
tls-options: Optional HTTPS with a generated self-signed certificate; no private CA or own certificate found
privacy-indicators: Light ring shows listening and mute state; hardware mute button
no-telemetry: Weekly anonymous ping cannot be turned off in 0.14.4; an off switch is merged to main for 0.14.5/0.15, unreleased
